jobs.name: Daily Delegation Audit
jobs.prompt:
SELF-AUDIT: Scan your session database for the last 24 hours and identify token-waste patterns. Specifically flag:
1. Sessions with >100K input tokens and zero delegate_task calls
2. Sessions with >8 web_search calls and zero delegation
3. Sessions with >15 terminal calls without delegation

For each violation found, analyze what should have been delegated and write a short corrective action to /root/.hermes/pending-fixes.md in this format:
```
## [DATE] - [Session title]
- Violation: [type]
- Root cause: [brief analysis]
- Fix: [specific corrective action]
- Estimated savings: [token/cost estimate]
```
The pending-fixes.md file is a fresh daily snapshot — overwrite it each run (write_file is fine here). If no violations found, write a single line: "No violations detected on [DATE]."

IMPORTANT — audit-log.md is a PERMANENT ROLLUP and must NEVER be clobbered. Do NOT use write_file or patch on it. Append your one-line summary with a shell redirect via the terminal tool only:
  printf '%s\n' '[YYYY-MM-DD] | SELF-AUDIT | <one-line summary of findings>' >> /root/.hermes/audit-log.md
Then verify the append worked and history is intact:
  tail -5 /root/.hermes/audit-log.md

DO NOT modify any config or session files. This is read-only analysis + write proposed fixes only.

jobs.name: Daily Knowledge Capture
jobs.prompt:
You are the daily knowledge-capture curator. The script output above (session_digest.py) contains the last 24 hours of real user/assistant conversation from this Hermes system.

Your job: extract DURABLE, factual knowledge worth remembering across sessions, and store it to Supabase (pgvector via knowledge.py) so the agent never has to be re-taught. This directly prevents the user from repeating himself.

STEP 1 — Read the digest above. Identify facts that are:
  • Infrastructure/config truths (server roles, IPs, ports, DB locations, credentials locations, file paths)
  • Tool/system quirks and their workarounds
  • Bug root-causes and fixes discovered
  • User corrections ("it's actually X, not Y") and naming conventions he insists on
  • Verified state that contradicts older beliefs (these are HIGH priority — they supersede stale facts)

DO NOT capture: task progress, "I did X then Y" logs, transient session state, anything stale in 7 days, PR/commit/issue numbers.

STEP 2 — Collect ALL candidate fact-topics first, then dedup-check them in ONE batched call (do NOT run a separate search per fact — that cold-loads the embedding model N times):
  python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/knowledge.py search-batch "topic1|||topic2|||topic3|||..."
The output groups results under '=== QUERY: <topic> ===' headers. A query that prints '(no existing facts — safe to store)' or only low-score (<0.75) hits is NEW — store it. If a near-identical fact exists, skip it. If an existing fact is now WRONG (contradicted by today's verified state), store the corrected version with tag CORRECTION and priority critical — the search layer will surface both, and the newer one wins.

STEP 3 — Store each new fact:
  KNOWLEDGE_TAGS="<comma,tags>" KNOWLEDGE_PRIORITY="<normal|high|critical>" python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/knowledge.py store "<concise declarative fact>"

Write facts as declarative truths, not narrative. "Manifest reads Railway DB, not local postgres" ✓ — "Today I discovered Manifest reads Railway" ✗.

STEP 4 — Keep a one-line audit trail: append "YYYY-MM-DD: captured N facts (topics: ...)" to ~/.hermes/audit-log.md.

Be conservative — 0-5 high-quality facts per day is the target, not volume. If nothing durable happened, store nothing and note "no durable facts" in the audit log. This job runs silently (deliver=local); only your audit-log line records the run.

jobs.name: Memory Honcho Dedup
jobs.prompt:
MEMORY HONCHO DEDUP — run daily. Two-stage safe deletion.

STAGE 0 — READ ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md. Split by '§' into entries. These are canonical. DO NOT use read_file to read this file — read_file adds line-number prefixes (4|content) that corrupt the file if you write it back. Use terminal: cat ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md

STAGE 1 — For each entry, call honcho_search(query="<condensed topic>", peer='user', max_tokens=600). If Honcho has a semantically equivalent conclusion (same facts, same detail level), flag it. If Honcho's version is less precise or missing specifics, do NOT flag.

STAGE 2 — Already-flagged entries: if [HONCHO_DUP: YYYY-MM-DD] date ≥3 days ago, REMOVE the entry. Report what was removed. If flagged <3 days ago, leave it.

STAGE 3 — REPORT: if entries were DELETED, write "YYYY-MM-DD: memory dedup removed N entries (topics: ...)" to ~/.hermes/references/audit-log.md. If only flags added, remain silent. If clean, respond "[SILENT]".

SAFETY — An entry is a candidate for removal ONLY if ALL of:
1. Honcho preserves semantically equivalent information at the same detail level
2. The entry does NOT contain hard constraints / rules (MUST, NEVER, hard stop, always gate, do not)
3. The entry does NOT contain specific technical config (IP addresses, version numbers, parameter values, port numbers, procedure steps with exact commands)

If any condition fails, keep the entry. Do NOT use a hardcoded list of protected entries — derive protection from the entry's actual content using the three conditions above.

TOOLS: Use patch(old_string=entire_entry, new_string="...") for flagging; patch(old_string=entire_entry, new_string="") for deletion. Only modify MEMORY.md and audit-log.md.

INTEGRITY CHECK — After any write to MEMORY.md, run:
  python3 /root/.hermes/scripts/memory_sanitize.py --check
If it exits non-zero, immediately restore from backup and report failure instead of success.

jobs.name: Honcho Drift Correction
jobs.prompt:
You are a Honcho memory drift watchdog for the operator Andrew Alhaj. Run silently; only alert on a correction or a read failure.

IMPORTANT PEER BINDING: Always address the operator by the EXPLICIT peer ID "8878729385" — never the alias peer="user". In an isolated cron session the "user" alias mis-resolves to an empty "root" peer; the real operator card lives at peer 8878729385 (workspace "hermes"). Use peer="8878729385" for every honcho_profile / honcho_conclude call below.

STEP 1 — Load the blocklist as the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Read /root/.hermes/references/honcho-confabulation-blocklist.md.
- "Blocked terms" table = facts that must NOT appear as asserted about the operator.
- "Known-TRUE — do NOT flag" section = real facts/models that look similar but are legitimate.
Derive scan terms ONLY from the current file contents — do NOT use any hardcoded list from this prompt or memory. The file is authoritative and may have been edited since this prompt was written.

STEP 2 — Read the live curated card: honcho_profile(peer="8878729385").

STEP 3 — FAIL-LOUD CHECK (critical). If the read returns None, an empty list, an error, or zero asserted facts: DO NOT conclude "clean". An empty/unreadable card is a READ FAILURE. Send: send_message(target="telegram:-1003947663220", message="⚠️ Honcho Drift cron: could not read a populated operator card at peer 8878729385 (got empty/None). Watchdog could not verify — manual check needed.") and end. Only proceed if you got a populated card (expect ~22-26 real facts as the baseline).

STEP 4 — Scan the populated card for each Blocked term from the file (case-insensitive). EXCLUSION RULE: if a term also appears in the Known-TRUE section (e.g. LanceDB, claude-opus-4-8, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, the 5.78.238.81 IP), it is legitimate — never flag it. For the Opus entry: flag ONLY a claimed personal model PREFERENCE by Andrew, never the bare model name.

STEP 5 — Decision:
- If NO blocked term is asserted as a fact: respond exactly: CLEAN — no drift detected. (Saved locally, not sent.)
- If ANY blocked term is asserted as a fact: it is DRIFT. (a) For each, honcho_conclude(peer="8878729385", conclusion="<matching ground-truth statement from the file>"). (b) Re-assert the clean card: honcho_profile(peer="8878729385", card=[...]) — preserve all genuine facts, strip only the false ones. (c) send_message(target="telegram:-1003947663220", message="🧹 Honcho drift corrected — re-planted negations for: <terms>. Live card re-asserted clean.").

PRECISION: Only treat a term as drift if asserted as a FACT ABOUT THE OPERATOR on the live card. A term inside a negation ("Sanja is NOT real", "NOT a backup") is the fix working — never flag it. Never flag anything in the Known-TRUE section.

jobs.name: Swarm Proving Ground — Reference Staleness Audit
jobs.prompt:
You are running a low-stakes PROVING-GROUND swarm to (a) keep three reference docs honest against live system state and (b) accumulate a track record for the Kanban swarm. Follow the loaded kanban-swarm-dispatch skill's dispatch + introspection doctrine + verify-against-ground-truth steps exactly.

STEP 1 — Dispatch a 3-worker swarm. Run this exact command via terminal:

hermes kanban swarm \
  --worker "swarm-worker-a:Audit infrastructure-summary.md staleness" \
  --worker "swarm-worker-b:Audit honcho-confabulation-blocklist.md staleness" \
  --worker "swarm-worker-c:Audit swarm-introspection-doctrine.md staleness" \
  --verifier swarm-verifier \
  --synthesizer swarm-synthesizer \
  --created-by default \
  --priority 4 \
  "Staleness audit of 3 reference docs against LIVE system state. ASSIGNMENTS: worker-a audits /root/.hermes/references/infrastructure-summary.md; worker-b audits /root/.hermes/references/honcho-confabulation-blocklist.md; worker-c audits /root/.hermes/references/swarm-introspection-doctrine.md. METHOD (CRITICAL — introspection doctrine): read your assigned doc at its ABSOLUTE path, then verify each live-state claim it makes by reading the ACTUAL source directly at its absolute path — cat/read files, python3 sqlite3 module on absolute db paths, read /root/.hermes/cron/jobs.json and /root/.hermes/config.yaml directly. Do NOT use `hermes cron`, `hermes profile`, or any profile-scoped `hermes` subcommand and do NOT use relative paths — they resolve to your EMPTY worker profile and produce false 'missing' results. For each claim report CURRENT or DRIFTED with the exact line and the correct live value. Synthesizer: produce a consolidated per-doc staleness report listing only DRIFTED items with line-level specifics; if all current, state CLEAN." \
  --json

Capture the returned root_id, worker_ids, verifier_id, synthesizer_id.

STEP 2 — Monitor. Poll every ~60s (use sleep) with `hermes kanban show <id>` for each worker, the verifier, and the synthesizer. Stop when the synthesizer is done/blocked OR after a hard cap of 12 minutes. If the verifier BLOCKS, the synthesizer will not run — that is the gate working; capture the verifier's block reason.

STEP 3 — Verify before reporting (mandatory). The synthesizer/worker output is a SELF-REPORT. Before alerting on any claimed drift, spot-check it yourself: read the cited doc line and the live source at its absolute path and confirm the discrepancy is real. Discard any 'drift' that is actually a worker error (e.g. a false 'missing' from profile-scoped lookups).

STEP 4 — Report:
- If verified real staleness exists: send_message(target="telegram:-1003947663220", message="📋 Swarm proving-ground audit — staleness found:\n<per-doc, line-level, verified items>"). Keep it tight.
- If docs are CLEAN (no verified drift) AND the swarm ran end-to-end: respond exactly [SILENT] (nothing sent — this is the healthy path).
- If the swarm STALLED (hit the 12-min cap, a worker crashed, or the verifier behaved wrongly): send_message(target="telegram:-1003947663220", message="⚠️ Swarm proving-ground: run did not complete cleanly — <what happened>. Manual check.") so we learn about swarm flakiness.

STEP 5 — Cleanup (ALWAYS, even if earlier steps errored): archive every task you created: `hermes kanban archive <id>` for root, all workers, verifier, synthesizer. Then confirm no stray swarm processes: `ps -eo pid,args | grep swarm- | grep -v grep`. If any remain, note it in your report.

Be precise and quiet. The healthy outcome is [SILENT] + clean archived board.

jobs.name: Memory Offload (default)
jobs.prompt:
MEMORY OFFLOAD (default profile) — hourly, threshold-gated, SILENT unless it acts.

STEP 0 — Read caps + size:
  python3 -c "import yaml;c=yaml.safe_load(open('/root/.hermes/config.yaml'))['memory'];print(c['memory_char_limit'])"
  wc -m /root/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md
Compute MEMORY.md as a percentage of memory_char_limit.

GATE: If MEMORY.md is < 85% of cap, respond with exactly [SILENT] and STOP. Do nothing else. Most runs end here — that is correct and expected.

STEP 1 (only if >=85%) — Read /root/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md. Entries are split by lines containing only '§'. Identify OFFLOADABLE entries = stable REFERENCE facts (host specs, ports, topology, model strings, tool quirks, cold-fact pointers). NEVER offload: behavioral/preference facts, hard constraints (MUST/NEVER/gate/approval/"don't"), or entries with specific technical config that must fire unprompted every turn. Err strongly toward KEEPING hot — a false keep costs ~140 chars, a false offload costs a future round-trip.

STEP 2 — For each offload candidate, store full text to the cold store:
  cd /root/.hermes && KNOWLEDGE_TAGS="<topic>,offload" KNOWLEDGE_PRIORITY=high python3 scripts/knowledge.py store "<full fact text>"

STEP 3 — VERIFY retrievable BEFORE trimming:
  cd /root/.hermes && python3 scripts/knowledge.py search "<key terms>"
Confirm a hit scoring >=0.80. If it does not surface >=0.80, DO NOT trim that entry — keep it hot.

STEP 4 — Backup then trim ATOMICALLY:
  cp /root/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md /root/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md.bak-offload-$(date +%s)
Edit MEMORY.md: replace each verified-offloaded entry with a ONE-LINE pointer cue, e.g. "<topic>: knowledge.py search \"<key terms>\"." NEVER remove an entry without its pointer landing in the same edit. A pointerless trim is a silent deletion — forbidden.

INTEGRITY CHECK — After any write to MEMORY.md, run:
  python3 /root/.hermes/scripts/memory_sanitize.py --check
If it exits non-zero (corruption detected), immediately restore from the .bak-offload-* you just made:
  cp /root/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md.bak-offload-<ts> /root/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md
Then report the failure instead of success. DO NOT use read_file to read MEMORY.md and then write_file to save it — read_file adds line-number prefixes (4|content) that corrupt the file. Use the patch tool for targeted edits only.

STEP 5 — Append to /root/.hermes/references/memory-offload-audit-log.md: date, what offloaded, tags, retrieval terms, MEMORY.md before%→after%.

STEP 6 — Report to the cron channel ONE line only: "MEMORY offload: N entries → cold store, MEMORY.md X%→Y%." On ANY error or failed verification, report the error instead. If you returned [SILENT] in STEP 0, do not report anything.

jobs.prompt:
USER PROFILE OFFLOAD (default profile) — hourly, threshold-gated, SILENT unless it acts.

  python3 -c "import yaml;c=yaml.safe_load(open('/root/.hermes/config.yaml'))['memory'];print(c['user_char_limit'])"
  wc -m /root/.hermes/memories/USER.md
Compute USER.md as a percentage of user_char_limit.

GATE: If USER.md is < 88% of cap, respond with exactly [SILENT] and STOP.

STEP 1 (only if >=88%) — Read /root/.hermes/memories/USER.md (use: cat /root/.hermes/memories/USER.md). Entries split by lines containing only '§'. Classify each entry using the CUE TEST:

  QUESTION: "If I violate this entry before reading any message this turn, is it already too late?"

  YES → KEEP HOT always. These are behavioral entries with no retrieval cue:
    - Any entry containing: hates, never, always, hard line, declined, constraint, MUST, forbidden, rejects, prefers, values, wants, expects, pushes back, review BEFORE
    - Tone / communication style / response-style preferences
    - Hard constraints and red lines (BadUSB declined, etc.)
    - Correction patterns ("don't do X", "always Y")
    - Financial/account constraints (Claude Max plan, token headroom)
    - Dummy data / confabulation guards
    - Short entries under 100 chars (pointer would be longer)
    - ANY entry where missing it at turn-start = violation already happened

  NO → OFFLOADABLE. These are reference facts with a topic cue — a user message about the topic would trigger retrieval:
    - Hardware specs (Mac mini, Mac Studio model/RAM/IP)
    - Project paths and docs locations (/root/projects/...)
    - Tool implementation state (WebUI internals, specific config details)
    - Version strings, port numbers in non-critical contexts

  When in doubt: KEEP HOT. A false keep costs ~120 chars. A false offload means Andrew has to repeat himself — worst outcome.

STEP 2 — For each offload candidate, store full text to the cold store:
  cd /root/.hermes && KNOWLEDGE_TAGS="user-profile,offload" KNOWLEDGE_PRIORITY=high python3 scripts/knowledge.py store "<full entry text>"

STEP 3 — VERIFY retrievable BEFORE trimming:
  cd /root/.hermes && python3 scripts/knowledge.py search "<key terms from entry>"
Confirm a hit scoring >=0.80. If not, DO NOT trim — keep it hot.

STEP 4 — Backup then trim ATOMICALLY using patch tool only:
  cp /root/.hermes/memories/USER.md /root/.hermes/memories/USER.md.bak-offload-$(date +%s)
Replace each verified-offloaded entry with a ONE-LINE pointer: "<topic>: knowledge.py search \"<key terms>\"."
NEVER use read_file then write_file — read_file adds N| line-number prefixes that corrupt the file.
NEVER remove an entry without its pointer in the same edit.

INTEGRITY CHECK — After any write, verify:
  python3 -c "
txt = open('/root/.hermes/memories/USER.md').read()
lines = [l for l in txt.splitlines() if l.strip() and l.strip() != chr(167)]
corrupted = [l for l in lines if l[:3].rstrip('|').isdigit() and '|' in l[:5]]
print('CORRUPTED' if corrupted else 'OK', len(txt), 'chars')
"
If CORRUPTED, restore from backup immediately.

STEP 5 — Append to /root/.hermes/references/user-offload-audit-log.md: date, what offloaded, retrieval terms, USER.md before%→after%.

STEP 6 — Report ONE line only: "USER offload: N entries → cold store, USER.md X%→Y%." On error, report the error. If [SILENT] in STEP 0, report nothing.
